gancho: Suba 12 quintas perfeitas e você deveria cair na mesma nota, sete oitavas acima. Não cai: sobra cerca de um quarto de semitom. Por isso o piano moderno deixa quase todos os intervalos levemente fora do "puro".
explicacao: Na afinação pitagórica, a quinta perfeita é o intervalo em que uma frequência vale 3/2 da outra, e a oitava é o dobro. Dando a volta no ciclo das quintas, 12 quintas deveriam coincidir com sete oitavas, mas a conta não fecha: as doze quintas sobem um pouco mais que as sete oitavas. A diferença, chamada coma pitagórica, é a razão 531441/524288, cerca de 1,01364, ou 23,46 cents, mais ou menos um quarto de semitom. Nesse sistema, notas que no teclado são a mesma tecla, como dó e si sustenido, ficam diferentes. Não há como ter, ao mesmo tempo, todas as quintas puras e as oitavas fechadas. A solução que domina a música ocidental desde o século XX é o temperamento igual: a oitava é dividida em 12 semitons exatamente iguais, cada um com a razão da raiz 12ª de 2, cerca de 1,05946. O preço é que os outros intervalos se afastam um pouco do som "puro". Quartas e quintas ficam mais perto do ideal; terças e sextas, mais longe.

fontes.trecho: the Pythagorean comma (or ditonic comma), named after the ancient mathematician and philosopher Pythagoras, is the small interval (or comma) existing in Pythagorean tuning between two enharmonically equivalent notes such as C and B♯, or D♭ and C♯. It is equal to the frequency ratio (1.5)12⁄27 = 531441⁄524288 ≈ 1.01364, or about 23.46 cents, roughly a quarter of a semitone [...] the difference between 12 just perfect fifths and seven octaves [...] A just perfect fifth has a frequency ratio of 3:2. [...] The Pythagorean comma can also be thought of as the discrepancy between 12 justly tuned perfect fifths (ratio 3:2) and seven octaves (ratio 2:1)

The most common equal temperament represents the octave as 12 exactly equal semitones. The 12-note chromatic scale employs a semitone ratio equal to the 12th root of 2 (212 ≈ 1.05946). Equalizing the semitones in this way causes other intervals to deviate slightly from their "pure" sounds; the fourths and fifths produced by this method are closer to their just intonation than the thirds and sixths are. Equal temperament has been the predominant tuning system of Western music since the 20th century.

gancho: A divisão da oitava em 12 semitons iguais, que domina a música ocidental, foi calculada com precisão em 1584 por um príncipe chinês, Zhu Zaiyu. Na China, o feito não teve reconhecimento oficial nem em vida dele.
explicacao: Zhu Zaiyu viveu de 1536 a 1611 e era descendente, em sexta geração, de um imperador da dinastia Ming. Herdou o título de príncipe de Zheng em 1593, mas logo abriu mão dele em favor de um primo. Passou trinta anos estudando uma ideia que vinha do pai: afinar com todos os semitons iguais. O método era dividir o comprimento da corda ou do tubo, passo a passo, pela raiz 12ª de 2, cerca de 1,059463. Depois de doze divisões, o comprimento cai pela metade, e a nota sobe exatamente uma oitava. Em 1584 ele publicou a especificação numérica. Para demonstrar a teoria, descreveu 36 tubos de bambu afinados, cobrindo três oitavas, com o tipo de bambu, a cor da tinta e os diâmetros. Em 1890, Victor-Charles Mahillon, curador do museu do Conservatório de Bruxelas, reproduziu os tubos e atestou a precisão da teoria. Na Europa, o flamengo Simon Stevin chegou a uma solução independente, um pouco menos precisa, num manuscrito publicado só em 1884. Na China, nem a dinastia Ming nem a Qing reconheceram oficialmente o trabalho, porque valorizavam a interpretação de textos clássicos acima de ideias baseadas na observação.

fontes.trecho: Zhu Zaiyu (Chinese: 朱載堉; 1536 – 19 May 1611) was a Chinese scholar, mathematician and music theorist. He was a prince of the Chinese Ming dynasty. In 1584, Zhu innovatively described the equal temperament via accurate mathematical calculation. [...] the sixth-generation descendant of the Hongxi Emperor, the fourth emperor of the Ming Dynasty. Zhu inherited the title the Prince of Zheng in 1593, but quickly resigned it to his cousin. [...] Zhu's work on equal temperament did not get any official recognition during his lifetime nor during the Qing dynasty. This was due to the Ming and Qing emphasis on classical scholarship and discouragement of ideas based on empirical observation rather than textual interpretations.

Equal temperament has been the predominant tuning system of Western music since the 20th century. [...] Simon Stevin's independent solution came the following year and was slightly less precise. [...] Zhu Zaiyu (朱載堉), a prince of the Ming court, spent thirty years on research based on the equal temperament idea originally postulated by his father. [...] This was followed by the publication of a precise numerical specification for equal temperament [...] in 1584. [...] Zhu obtained his result mathematically by dividing the length of string and pipe successively by 12√2 ≈ 1.059463 [...] such that after twelve divisions (an octave) the length was divided by a factor of 2 [...] Zhu Zaiyu illustrated his equal temperament theory by the construction of a set of 36 bamboo tuning pipes ranging in 3 octaves, with instructions of the type of bamboo, color of paint, and detailed specification on their length and inner and outer diameters. [...] In 1890, Victor-Charles Mahillon, curator of the Conservatoire museum in Brussels, duplicated a set of pitch pipes according to Zhu Zaiyu's specification. [...] the set of pipes duplicated according to the Zaiyu data proved the accuracy of this theory. [...] in Simon Stevin's manuscript Vande Spiegheling der singconst (On the Theory of the Art of Singing, c. 1605), published posthumously nearly three centuries later in 1884.

gancho: Telefones tradicionais não reproduzem sons abaixo de 300 Hz, e a voz masculina tem a frequência fundamental perto de 150 Hz. Mesmo assim, você a ouve no tom certo: o cérebro deduz a nota que falta pelos harmônicos.
explicacao: Um som de instrumento ou de voz não é uma frequência única. Uma nota de 100 Hz, por exemplo, vem acompanhada de componentes em múltiplos dela: 200, 300, 400 Hz e assim por diante. Se a componente de 100 Hz é retirada, o ouvinte continua percebendo a altura de 100 Hz. É a chamada fundamental ausente. Por um tempo se achou que o próprio ouvido recriava a frequência por distorção, mas em 1954 J. C. R. Licklider relatou que, mesmo com um ruído capaz de encobrir essas distorções, as pessoas ainda ouviam a nota que faltava. Hoje é amplamente aceito que o cérebro calcula a fundamental a partir dos padrões de repetição dos harmônicos, embora o mecanismo exato ainda seja debatido. O truque está por toda parte. As notas mais graves do violino têm a fundamental fraca, e quase ninguém nota. Um tímpano pode soar forte em 200, 302, 398 e 488 Hz, sugerindo uma fundamental de 100 Hz. Alguns órgãos de tubos usam o efeito para tirar notas muito graves de tubos menores, e fabricantes de áudio o usam para que caixas de som pareçam tocar mais grave do que conseguem. A percepção, porém, varia de pessoa para pessoa.

fontes.trecho: The missing fundamental phenomenon is the perceptual phenomenon of hearing a pitch corresponding to the lowest (fundamental) harmonic when presented with sound made of a set of frequency multiples (overtones), even when it is actually absent. [...] For example, when a note (that is not a pure tone) has a pitch of 100 Hz, it will consist of frequency components that are integer multiples of that value (e.g. 100, 200, 300, 400, 500.... Hz). However, smaller loudspeakers may not produce low frequencies, so in our example, the 100 Hz component may be missing. Nevertheless, a pitch corresponding to the fundamental may still be heard. [...] This perception is due to the brain interpreting repetition patterns that are present. It was once thought that this effect was because the missing fundamental was replaced by distortions introduced by the physics of the ear. However, experiments subsequently showed that when a noise was added that would have masked these distortions had they been present, listeners still heard a pitch corresponding to the missing fundamental, as reported by J. C. R. Licklider in 1954. It is now widely accepted that the brain processes the information present in the overtones to calculate the fundamental frequency. The precise way in which it does so is still a matter of debate [...] A 2013 study by D. Robert Ladd et al. finds that sensitivity to perceive missing fundamental varies across individuals. [...] A timpani might be tuned to produce sound most strongly at 200, 302, 398, and 488 Hz, for instance, implying a missing fundamental at 100 Hz [...] so the lowest notes of a violin have an attenuated fundamental, although listeners seldom notice this. Most common telephones cannot reproduce sounds lower than 300 Hz, but a male voice has a fundamental frequency of approximately 150 Hz. Because of the missing fundamental effect, the fundamental frequencies of male voices are still perceived as their pitches over the telephone. The missing fundamental phenomenon is used electronically by some pro audio manufacturers to allow sound systems to seem to produce notes that are lower in pitch than they are capable of reproducing. [...] Some pipe organs make use of this phenomenon as a resultant tone, which allows relatively smaller bass pipes to produce very low-pitched sounds.

gancho: Há pares de notas que umas pessoas ouvem subir e outras ouvem descer, cada uma quase sempre do mesmo jeito. A pesquisadora que descobriu o efeito ligou isso à língua e ao sotaque de quem ouve, ideia ainda debatida.
explicacao: São tons de Shepard: cada nota é feita de vários tons puros separados por oitavas, com o volume moldado de forma que não dá para dizer em que oitava ela está. Em 1963, Roger Shepard argumentou que dois desses tons separados por meia oitava, o trítono, seriam ouvidos de forma ambígua, ora subindo, ora descendo. Em 1986, porém, Diana Deutsch analisou cada ouvinte separadamente e viu que o julgamento dependia da posição das notas no círculo cromático. Uma pessoa ouvia dó–fá sustenido subindo e sol–dó sustenido descendo; outra, o contrário. Como isso exige reagir à altura absoluta das notas, o achado foi usado para defender que muita gente tem um ouvido absoluto latente. Deutsch relatou ainda que ouvintes do sul da Inglaterra e da Califórnia resolvem a ambiguidade de jeitos opostos, e que falantes nativos de vietnamita, uma língua tonal, ouvem diferente dos californianos que falam inglês. A ligação com a origem linguística foi reproduzida numa amostra canadense e em amostras fora dos EUA, mas alguns estudos, comparando alemães com japoneses ou britânicos com holandeses e americanos, não acharam diferenças sistemáticas.

fontes.trecho: The tritone paradox is an auditory illusion in which a sequentially played pair of Shepard tones  separated by an interval of a tritone, or half octave, is heard as ascending by some people and as descending by others. [...] Roger Shepard in 1963 had argued that such tone pairs would be heard ambiguously as either ascending or descending. However, psychology of music researcher Diana Deutsch in 1986 discovered that when the judgments of individual listeners were considered separately, their judgments depended  on the positions of the tones along the  chromatic circle. For example, one listener would hear the tone pair C–F♯ as ascending and the tone pair G–C♯ as descending. Yet another listener would hear the tone pair C–F♯ as descending and the tone pair G–C♯ as ascending. Furthermore, the way these tone pairs were perceived varied depending on the listener's language or dialect. Each Shepard tone consists of a set of octave-related sinusoids, whose amplitudes are scaled by a fixed bell-shaped spectral envelope based on a log frequency scale. [...] an individual will usually find the same tone to be higher, and this is determined by the tones' absolute pitches. [...] This finding has been used to argue that latent absolute-pitch ability is present in a large proportion of the population.  In addition, Deutsch found that subjects from the south of England and from California resolved the ambiguity the opposite way. Also, Deutsch, Henthorn and Dolson found that native speakers of Vietnamese, a tonal language, heard the tritone paradox differently from Californians who were native speakers of English.

fontes.titulo: Frontiers in Psychology (2018): artigo sobre o paradoxo do trítono
fontes.trecho: Differences in the tritone paradox for different linguistic backgrounds were also replicated in a Canadian sample (highest pitch class at G, Dawe et al., 1998). [...] The influence of language on the tritone paradox was also replicated in samples outside the US [...] However, some studies failed to reveal systematic differences in subjectively highest Shepard tones for different linguistic backgrounds, for example, Krüger and Lukas (2002), who compared German and Japanese samples and Repp (1994), who compared British, Dutch, and American samples.

gancho: Repita certas frases faladas várias vezes, sem mudar nada no áudio, e elas passam a soar cantadas. A pesquisadora Diana Deutsch notou o efeito por acaso, em 1995, enquanto preparava os comentários de um CD.
explicacao: Deutsch tinha deixado em loop a frase em inglês "sometimes behave so strangely" (às vezes se comportam de modo tão estranho) e percebeu que, depois de algumas repetições, ela parecia cantada. Mais tarde, notou que, uma vez transformada em canção, a frase continuava soando cantada mesmo dentro da sentença completa. Num experimento com colegas, quem ouvia a frase uma vez a repetia falando; quem a ouvia dez vezes a repetia cantando. A mudança só acontecia com repetições idênticas. Se as cópias eram levemente transpostas, ou se as sílabas vinham embaralhadas, nada feito. Nem toda frase funciona: as que têm sílabas de altura mais estável e um ritmo que lembra compasso favorecem a ilusão. Exames de imagem mostraram mais atividade em áreas dos lobos frontais e temporais, nos dois lados do cérebro, quando a frase era percebida como canto. A ilusão aparece em pessoas com e sem formação musical e em falantes de várias línguas, inclusive o português, mas é mais fraca entre falantes de línguas tonais, como o tailandês e o mandarim. Uma explicação proposta é que, na fala, o cérebro abafa um pouco a percepção da altura das sílabas para se concentrar nas consoantes e vogais. A repetição exata soltaria esse freio, e as alturas passariam a se destacar como notas.

fontes.trecho: The speech-to-song illusion is an auditory illusion discovered by Diana Deutsch in 1995. A spoken phrase is repeated several times, without altering it in any way, and without providing any context. This repetition causes the phrase to transform perceptually from speech into song. [...] The illusion was discovered by Deutsch in 1995 when she was preparing the spoken commentary on her CD ‘Musical Illusions and Paradoxes'. She had the phrase ‘sometimes behave so strangely' on a loop, and noticed that after it had been repeated several times it appeared to be sung rather than spoken. [...] noted that once the phrase had perceptually morphed into song, it continued to be heard as song when played in the context of the full sentence in which it occurred. [...] This perceptual transformation required that the intervening repetitions be exact; it did not occur when they were transposed slightly, or presented with the syllables in jumbled orderings. In addition, when listeners were asked to repeat back the phrase after hearing it once, they repeated it back as speech. Yet when they were asked to repeat back the phrase after hearing it ten times, they repeated it back as song. [...] Increased activation has been found in the frontal and temporal lobes of both hemispheres when the listener was perceiving a repeated spoken phrase as sung rather than spoken. [...] The speech-to-song illusion occurs in listeners both with and without musical training. It occurs in listeners who speak different languages, including the non-tone languages English, Irish, Catalan, German, Italian, Portuguese, French, Croatian, and Hindi, and the tone languages Thai and Mandarin; however, it is weaker in speakers of tone languages than non-tone languages. [...] It has been suggested that in speech the neural circuitry underlying pitch perception is somewhat inhibited, enabling the listener to focus attention on consonants and vowels, which are important to verbal meaning. Exact repetition of spoken words may cause this circuitry to become disinhibited, so that pitches are heard more saliently, and so as sung. [...] Phrases that are marked by syllables with stable pitches and that favor a metrical interpretation tend to be conducive to the illusion.

gancho: Num teste às cegas, dez solistas renomados não distinguiram violinos italianos antigos, quase todos Stradivarius, de violinos novos melhor do que no chute. Seis deles escolheram um novo para uma turnê hipotética.
explicacao: Há muitas teorias para o som dos Stradivarius, da madeira crescida na Pequena Idade do Gelo ao verniz, mas nenhuma pesquisa explicou ou reproduziu de forma conclusiva a qualidade atribuída a eles. Testes às cegas feitos desde o século XIX frequentemente não acharam diferença significativa em relação a bons violinos modernos. Num teste famoso da rádio BBC, em 1977, os violinistas Isaac Stern e Pinchas Zukerman e um especialista tentaram reconhecer quatro instrumentos tocados atrás de uma tela. Nenhum acertou mais de dois, e dois deles apontaram o violino do século XX como o Stradivarius. Os críticos lembravam que esses testes raramente eram duplo-cegos. Num estudo publicado na revista PNAS, dez solistas testaram às cegas seis violinos antigos italianos, cinco deles de Stradivari, e seis novos, em duas sessões de 75 minutos: uma numa sala de ensaio e outra numa sala de concerto de 300 lugares. Seis dos dez escolheram um instrumento novo para substituir o próprio numa turnê imaginária, e um violino novo foi de longe o preferido. Em média, os novos favoritos ganharam em facilidade de tocar, articulação e projeção, e ficaram pelo menos empatados em timbre. Em 2017, outro estudo voltou a preferir os modernos.

fontes.titulo: Soloist evaluations of six Old Italian and six new violins (Fritz et al., PNAS, via HAL)
fontes.trecho: In this study, 10 renowned soloists each blind-tested six Old Italian violins (including five by Stradivari) and six new during two 75-min sessions-the first in a rehearsal room, the second in a 300-seat concert hall. When asked to choose a violin to replace their own for a hypothetical concert tour, 6 of the 10 soloists chose a new instrument. A single new violin was easily the most-preferred of the 12. On average, soloists rated their favorite new violins more highly than their favorite old for playability, articulation, and projection, and at least equal to old in terms of timbre. Soloists failed to distinguish new from old at better than chance levels.

theories ranging from the unique quality of the wood used during the Little Ice Age to the varnishes and chemical treatments applied. Despite extensive scientific research, including modern acoustic analysis and CT scans, no one has conclusively replicated or fully explained the tonal qualities of Stradivarius instruments. [...] Blind experiments conducted since the 19th century have often found no significant difference between Stradivari instruments and high-quality modern violins. [...] In a particularly famous test on a BBC Radio 3 programme in 1977, the violinists Isaac Stern and Pinchas Zukerman and the violin expert and dealer Charles Beare tried to distinguish between the "Chaconne" Stradivarius, a 1739 Guarneri del Gesú, an 1846 Vuillaume, and a 1976 British violin played behind a screen by a professional soloist. [...] None of the listeners identified more than two of the four instruments. Two of the listeners identified the 20th-century violin as the Stradivarius. Violinists and others have criticized these tests on various grounds such as that they are not double-blind (in most cases) [...] Modern violins were rated as having better sound-carrying qualities and were preferred again in a study in 2017.

gancho: Acordes "dissonantes", que soam ásperos para nós, agradaram tanto quanto os consonantes aos Tsimane', povo da Amazônia boliviana com pouco contato com música ocidental. O gosto pela consonância parece aprendido.
explicacao: Desde os gregos se nota que intervalos agradáveis ao ouvido ocidental, como a quinta, têm razões simples entre as frequências das notas, como 3:2. Por isso, alguns cientistas supunham que o cérebro já nasce preferindo esses acordes. Testar isso é difícil, porque quase todo mundo hoje ouve muita música pop ocidental. Os Tsimane', sociedade de agricultores e coletores de cerca de 12 mil pessoas, são uma exceção, sobretudo os que vivem longe das cidades. Na música deles, em geral só uma pessoa canta ou toca por vez. Em 2011 e 2015, pesquisadores do MIT e da Universidade Brandeis pediram a mais de 100 Tsimane' que avaliassem acordes. Entre eles, a preferência pela consonância foi indetectável. Ela foi pequena entre bolivianos de uma cidadezinha próxima e da capital, La Paz, maior entre americanos e maior ainda entre músicos americanos. Os Tsimane' distinguiam os dois tipos de som, reagiram como os outros grupos a risadas e arfadas e, como eles, não gostavam de sons acusticamente ásperos. Anos depois, o mesmo laboratório mostrou que eles, como moradores de Boston, confundem mais facilmente duas notas consonantes com um som só. Ou seja, parte da percepção dos intervalos pode ser universal, enquanto o prazer que eles dão seria cultural.

fontes.titulo: Why we like the music we do (MIT News, 2016)
fontes.trecho: A new study from MIT and Brandeis University suggests that the answer is no. [...] For centuries, some scientists have hypothesized that the brain is wired to respond favorably to consonant chords such as the fifth [...] For decades, neuroscientists have pondered whether this preference is somehow hardwired into our brains. [...] In a study of more than 100 people belonging to a remote Amazonian tribe with little or no exposure to Western music, the researchers found that dissonant chords such as the combination of C and F# were rated just as likeable as “consonant” chords [...] Musicians in societies dating at least as far back as the ancient Greeks noticed that in the fifth and other consonant chords, the ratio of frequencies of the two notes is usually based on integers — in the case of the fifth, a ratio of 3:2. [...] “It’s pretty hard to find people who don’t have a lot of exposure to Western pop music due to its diffusion around the world,” [...] Most of the Tsimane, a farming and foraging society of about 12,000 people, have very limited exposure to Western music. [...] Among the folks who live very far, several days away, they don’t have too much contact with Western music. [...] The Tsimane’s own music features both singing and instrumental performance, but usually by only one person at a time. [...] The researchers did two sets of studies, one in 2011 and one in 2015. [...] The researchers also performed experiments to make sure that the participants could tell the difference between dissonant and consonant sounds, and found that they could. The team performed the same tests with a group of Spanish-speaking Bolivians who live in a small town near the Tsimane, and residents of the Bolivian capital, La Paz. They also tested groups of American musicians and nonmusicians. [...] “In the Tsimane it’s undetectable, and in the two groups in Bolivia, there’s a statistically significant but small preference. In the American groups it’s quite a bit larger, and it’s bigger in the musicians than in the nonmusicians.” When asked to rate nonmusical sounds such as laughter and gasps, the Tsimane showed similar responses to the other groups. [...] They also showed the same dislike for a musical quality known as acoustic roughness.

fontes.titulo: MIT News (2020): percepção de intervalos musicais entre os Tsimane'
fontes.trecho: researchers in the McDermott lab at the McGovern Institute for Brain Research have found that aspects of the perception of note combinations may be universal, even though the aesthetic evaluation of note combination as pleasant or unpleasant is culture-specific. [...] They found that, like the Boston cohort, the Tsimane’ were more likely to mistake two notes as a single sound if they were consonant than if they were dissonant.

gancho: Achava-se que só humanos ajustavam o corpo ao ritmo de uma música. Então uma cacatua chamada Snowball, que dançava Backstreet Boys, passou num teste científico: acompanhava a batida mesmo com o andamento alterado.
explicacao: Snowball começou a balançar a cabeça ao som de "Everybody (Backstreet's Back)" na casa de um dono anterior. Em 2007, foi entregue a um abrigo de aves na Carolina do Sul, nos EUA, e a dona do abrigo pôs na internet um vídeo dele dançando, que passou de 200 mil visualizações numa semana. O neurocientista Aniruddh Patel disse que o queixo dele caiu ao ver o vídeo, e comparou a cena à de um cachorro lendo jornal em voz alta. Entre janeiro e maio de 2008, a equipe dele tocou a música favorita de Snowball em vários andamentos, para separar o ritmo de verdade da simples imitação de gestos humanos. O resultado: ele dançava espontaneamente e ajustava os movimentos ao andamento, ainda que dentro de certos limites. A dança não parece vir da exibição de corte da espécie, que é simples e breve. Patel sugeriu que a habilidade venha de uma ligação entre as áreas auditivas e motoras do cérebro, ligada à capacidade de aprender e imitar sons, que humanos e cacatuas têm. Em 2019, outro estudo registrou 14 passos diferentes, alguns talvez copiados de humanos e outros improvisados. Inspirados em estudos com cacatuas e papagaios, pesquisadores treinaram depois uma leoa-marinha, Ronan, que aprendeu a marcar o ritmo com a cabeça, inclusive em ritmos que nunca tinha ouvido, e já passou por mais de 2.000 sessões de treino.

fontes.trecho: noted as being the first non-human animal conclusively demonstrated to be capable of beat induction: perceiving music and synchronizing his body movements to the beat (i.e. dancing). [...] Snowball's abilities first became apparent after being acquired from a bird show at the age of six by his previous owner. He was observed bobbing his head in time to the Backstreet Boys song, "Everybody (Backstreet's Back)". [...] In August 2007, Snowball was relinquished by his previous owner (at least his third) to the Bird Lovers Only bird shelter of Duncan, South Carolina [...] Shelter owner Irena Schulz was informed of the cockatoo's unusual ability and, after confirming this behavior at first hand, uploaded a video of Snowball's dancing, swaying, and head bobbing to her website. [...] The video became an Internet phenomenon, with over 200,000 views in one week [...] Dr. Patel stated that his "jaw hit the floor" upon seeing the video, comparing the unlikely and contrary-to-accepted-wisdom nature of a cockatoo dancing to human music to that of a "dog reading a newspaper out loud". Between January and May 2008, Patel led research to determine whether or not Snowball was in fact truly synchronizing his body movements to the music (as opposed to simply mimicking or responding to visual clues from humans present in the room at the same time). Snowball's favorite piece of music was played to him at several different tempos and his reactions recorded on video for later analysis. [...] showed that Snowball was capable of spontaneously dancing to human music and also that he could adjust his movements to match the tempo of the music (albeit to a limited extent), a behavior previously thought only to occur in humans. This ability is believed to be unrelated to the male Eleonora cockatoo's natural courtship display, which is described as "simple and brief" [...] Patel has suggested that the capability of both humans and cockatoos to move synchronously to a rhythmic beat may be a "byproduct of a link between the auditory and motor parts of the brain" as a result of both species' ability to learn and mimic sounds. [...] In 2019, Patel published further research which indicated that Snowball demonstrated 14 different dance moves, some of which may have been copied from the humans around him and some spontaneously improvised.

Ronan is a sea lion who is known for being able to "dance" to music by moving her head and synchronizing her moves. [...] Starting in July 2011, at age three, she began training to bop her head to a metronome, inspired by similar studies on cockatoos and African gray parrots. [...] She has been trained in over 2,000 sessions. [...] She later began to do so to music as well, including rhythms she has not heard before.

gancho: Em 1784, Mozart comprou um estorninho e anotou a melodia que ele cantava: quase o tema de um concerto que o compositor terminara semanas antes, com dois "erros". Ao morrer, a ave ganhou enterro e poema.
explicacao: A anotação é de 27 de maio de 1784: "Estorninho, 34 kreuzer", seguida de "Que beleza!" e de uma melodia escrita à mão. Ela é bem parecida com o início do terceiro movimento do Concerto para Piano nº 17, K. 453, que Mozart concluíra em 12 de abril. Como o pássaro aprendeu a música não se sabe; a suposição mais comum é que o próprio Mozart a tenha ensinado na loja. Pela transcrição, o estorninho pôs uma pausa prolongada onde não havia e cantou sol sustenido no lugar de sol. Estorninhos são imitadores vocais muito hábeis, por isso a anotação provavelmente não era brincadeira. Para dois pesquisadores que estudaram esses pássaros, Meredith West e Andrew King, vários trechos de "Uma brincadeira musical", obra de Mozart de 1787, também trazem a "assinatura vocal" de um estorninho. A ave morreu em 4 de junho de 1787, depois de três anos com a família. Segundo relatos de biógrafos da época, Mozart a enterrou no jardim com cerimônia: um cortejo em que todos que sabiam cantar tinham de entrar, cobertos com véus, e um epitáfio em verso. Pouco antes, ele tinha perdido o pai.

fontes.trecho: For about three years, the composer Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart kept a pet starling. [...] The first record of the starling is the entry Mozart made in his expense book when he bought it on 27 May 1784: Starling bird 34 Kr. That was beautiful! The music Mozart jotted down in the book is fairly close to the opening bars of the third movement of his Piano Concerto No. 17 in G, K. 453, which Mozart had completed a few weeks earlier (12 April). Presumably, Mozart taught the bird to sing this tune in the pet store, or wherever it was that he bought it. According to Mozart's transcription, the starling incorrectly inserted a fermata on the last beat of the first full measure, and sang G♯ instead of G in the following measure. [...] Mozart probably was not joking when he made the transcription, because starlings are known to have a very strong capacity for vocal mimicry. To the ears of West and King, many elements of Mozart's A Musical Joke (1787) also "bear the vocal autograph of a starling". [...] The bird Mozart brought home lived as a pet in his household for three years and died on 4 June 1787. Mozart buried the creature in the garden with (as contemporary biographers observed) considerable ceremony. [...] When a bird died, he arranged a funeral procession, in which everyone who could sing had to join in, heavily veiled – made a sort of requiem, epitaph in verse. [...] His father had passed away, a close friend had died young

gancho: Um piano bem afinado não segue a escala matemática: os agudos ficam um pouco mais agudos e os graves mais graves do que a teoria manda. A culpa é da rigidez das cordas de aço, que desloca os harmônicos.
explicacao: Na teoria, duas notas estão a uma oitava quando a fundamental da mais aguda coincide com o segundo harmônico da mais grave, ou seja, com o dobro da frequência. Numa corda ideal, os harmônicos são múltiplos exatos da fundamental. Mas uma corda de aço de verdade resiste um pouco a se dobrar, e essa rigidez faz os harmônicos saírem ligeiramente mais altos, ainda mais nos harmônicos superiores. É a inarmonicidade. O afinador começa pelo meio do teclado e ajusta cada nova nota aos harmônicos das que já afinou, que estão um pouco altos. Assim, o desvio vai se acumulando até as pontas: as oitavas ficam "esticadas". Nos anos 1930, o professor de física O. L. Railsback mediu esse desvio em pianos afinados para soar bem e concluiu que ele não vinha de falta de precisão, e sim da inarmonicidade. Pianos pequenos, com cordas curtas e grossas, sofrem mais com isso; nos pianos de cauda, o efeito diminui muito. A inarmonicidade é até um dos limites práticos da extensão do teclado. Pianos elétricos antigos, como o Fender Rhodes, e sintetizadores que os imitam também usam essa afinação esticada.

fontes.trecho: Stretched tuning is a detail of musical tuning, applied to wire-stringed musical instruments, older, non-digital electric pianos (such as the Fender Rhodes piano and Wurlitzer electric piano), and some sample-based synthesizers based on these instruments, to accommodate the natural inharmonicity of their vibrating elements. In stretched tuning, two notes an octave apart, whose fundamental frequencies theoretically have an exact 2:1 ratio, are tuned slightly farther apart (a stretched octave). [...] we say two notes are an octave apart when the fundamental frequency of the upper note exactly matches the second harmonic of the lower note. [...] But on metal strings, tines, and reeds, the measured frequencies of those harmonics are slightly higher, and proportionately more so in the higher than in the lower harmonics. [...] On longer strings, such as on concert grand or even moderately sized grand pianos, this effect is greatly reduced.

Inharmonicity increases continuously as notes get further from the middle of the piano, and is one of the practical limits on the total range of the instrument. [...] The tuner stretches the notes, slightly sharpening the high notes and flatting the low notes to make overtones of lower notes have the same frequency as the fundamentals of higher notes. [...] The Railsback curve, first measured in the 1930s by O.L. Railsback, a US college physics teacher, expresses the difference between inharmonicity-aware stretched piano tuning, and theoretically correct equal-tempered tuning [...] The curve is derived empirically from actual pianos tuned to be pleasing to the ear, not from an exact mathematical equation. [...] Railsback discovered that pianos were typically tuned in this manner not because of a lack of precision, but because of inharmon [...] Inharmonicity in a string is caused primarily by stiffness. [...] Those previously tuned notes have overtones that are sharpened by inharmonicity, which causes the newly established pitch to conform to the sharpened overtone. As the tuning progresses up and down the scale, the inharmonicity, hence the stretch, accumulates. [...] because piano tuning normally starts in the middle.

gancho: Na reunião de 1939 que firmou o lá de 440 Hz como padrão, prevaleceu o argumento de um engenheiro britânico: 439, o padrão dos afinadores ingleses, é primo, e 440 é mais fácil de gerar eletronicamente.
explicacao: O 440 já tinha história. Em 1834, o alemão Johann Heinrich Scheibler, inventor de um aparelho para medir a altura das notas, o recomendou, e um encontro de cientistas em Stuttgart o aprovou. Mas a França tinha seu padrão de 435 Hz, adotado por muitos países, e os afinadores britânicos usavam 439 desde 1899. A indústria musical americana chegou a 440 por conta própria em 1926. Em maio de 1939, delegados de França, Alemanha, Holanda, Itália e Inglaterra se reuniram na sede da BBC, em Londres, e aceitaram a posição do engenheiro e músico amador James Swinburne: 439 é primo, e 440 se decompõe com facilidade e é mais fácil de sintetizar eletronicamente. A ISO adotou a recomendação em 1955 e a formalizou em 1975. Nem todos seguem: orquestras da Europa continental costumam afinar entre 440 e 444 Hz. Neste século, sites e vídeos passaram a defender o lá de 432 Hz, a chamada "afinação Verdi", com alegações enganosas de poderes de cura e teorias da conspiração segundo as quais os nazistas teriam favorecido o 440. O padrão, porém, já tinha sido recomendado em 1834, muito antes dos nazistas.

fontes.trecho: Johann Heinrich Scheibler recommended A440 as a standard in 1834 after inventing the "tonometer" to measure pitch, and it was approved by the Society of German Natural Scientists and Physicians at a meeting in Stuttgart the same year. During the same era, in the 1860s, the French established a standard of 435 Hz, which was adopted by many countries and organizations. [...] The American music industry reached an informal standard of 440 Hz in 1926 [...] In 1937 Sir James Swinburne, an electrical engineer and avid amateur musician [...] British piano tuners had adopted A439 as the standard in 1899, but Swinburne pointed out that 439 was a prime number, whereas 440 could be more easily factored and electronically synthesized. In May 1939, delegates from France, Germany, The Netherlands, Italy, and England convened at Broadcasting House in London, the headquarters of the BBC, to address the issue of concert pitch. [...] The other European delegates concurred with Swinburne's position and agreed to a standard of A440. This standard was taken up by the International Organization for Standardization in 1955 as Recommendation R 16, before being formalised in 1975 as ISO 16. [...] In continental Europe the frequency of A4 commonly varies between 440 Hz and 444 Hz.

Particularly in the beginning of the 21st century, many websites and online videos have been published arguing for the adoption of the 432 Hz tuning – often referred to as "Verdi pitch" – instead of the predominant 440 Hz. These claims also include conspiracy theories, related to specious claims of healing properties from 432 Hz pitch, or involving Nazis having favored the 440 Hz tuning.

gancho: O inventor do teremim, um dos primeiros instrumentos eletrônicos, tocado com a mão no ar, também criou um grampo espião que passou sete anos numa réplica do Grande Selo dos EUA, no escritório do embaixador em Moscou.
explicacao: Lev Termen, conhecido no Ocidente como Leon Theremin, viveu de 1896 a 1993. Num instituto de pesquisa onde entrou a convite de Ioffe, construiu um oscilador para medir propriedades elétricas de gases e, ao acrescentar um circuito que gerava som, notou que a altura do tom mudava quando ele mexia a mão perto do aparelho. Mostrou a descoberta a Ioffe em outubro de 1920 e, no mês seguinte, deu o primeiro concerto público com o instrumento. Em 1938, ele voltou de repente à União Soviética. Na época, houve quem dissesse que foi sequestrado; anos depois, veio à tona que ele enfrentava problemas financeiros e com impostos nos Estados Unidos, embora ele próprio tenha contado a Bulat Galeyev que saiu por medo da guerra que se aproximava. Lá, foi preso e mandado às minas de ouro de Kolyma, e depois a uma "sharashka", laboratório secreto do sistema de campos do Gulag, ao lado de nomes como Andrei Tupolev e Sergei Korolev. Nesse período, criou um sistema de escuta que lhe valeu o Prêmio Stalin em 1947. Também inventou "A Coisa", um grampo escondido numa réplica do Grande Selo dos EUA entalhada em madeira. Em 1945, crianças soviéticas deram o presente ao embaixador americano como "gesto de amizade". A peça captou conversas nos primeiros sete anos da Guerra Fria, até ser descoberta por acaso em 1952, e é vista como uma precursora da tecnologia RFID.

fontes.trecho: Lev Sergeyevich Termen (28 August [O.S. 16 August] 1896 – 3 November 1993), better known as Leon Theremin, was a Russian inventor, most famous for his invention of the theremin, one of the first electronic musical instruments [...] His secret listening device, "The Thing", hung for seven years in plain view in the United States ambassador's Moscow office and enabled Soviet agents to secretly eavesdrop on conversations. [...] The day after Ioffe's invitation, Theremin started at the institute. [...] He built a high-frequency oscillator to measure the dielectric constant of gases with high precision [...] While adapting the dielectric device by adding circuitry to generate an audio tone, Theremin noticed that the pitch changed when his hand moved around. In October 1920 he first demonstrated this to Ioffe who called in other professors and students to hear. [...] By November 1920, Theremin had given his first public concert with the instrument [...] Theremin abruptly returned to the Soviet Union in 1938. At the time, the reasons for his return were unclear; some claimed that he was homesick, while others believed that he had been kidnapped by Soviet officials. [...] Shortly after he returned he was imprisoned in the Butyrka prison and later sent to work in the Kolyma gold mines. [...] Theremin was put to work in a sharashka (a secret laboratory in the Gulag camp system), together with Andrei Tupolev, Sergei Korolev and other well-known scientists and engineers. [...] In 1947, Theremin was awarded the Stalin prize for inventing this advance in Soviet espionage technology. Theremin invented another listening device called The Thing, hidden in a replica of the Great Seal of the United States carved in wood. In 1945, Soviet school children presented the concealed bug to the U.S. Ambassador as a "gesture of friendship" to the USSR's World War II ally. It hung in the ambassador’s residential office in Moscow and intercepted confidential conversations there during the first seven years of the Cold War, until it was accidentally discovered in 1952. [...] it is considered a predecessor of RFID technology [...] Many years later, it was revealed that Theremin had returned to his native land due to tax and financial difficulties in the United States. However, Theremin himself once told Bulat Galeyev that he decided to leave himself because he was anxious about the approaching war.

gancho: Existe um som que parece subir para sempre sem nunca ficar mais agudo: o tom de Shepard. O truque, com notas separadas por oitavas que surgem e somem aos poucos, está na trilha de "Dunkirk" e em "Super Mario 64".
explicacao: Cada tom de Shepard é a soma de tons puros separados por oitavas. Numa escala que sobe, todos sobem juntos, meio tom por vez. O componente mais agudo vai perdendo volume até sumir, enquanto um novo entra, quase inaudível, uma oitava abaixo. Como o volume de cada componente cresce e some aos poucos, o ouvido nunca percebe onde a escala começa ou termina. Depois de doze passos, o som volta a ser igual ao primeiro, e o ciclo recomeça. Num programa de ciência da BBC, o efeito foi chamado de "poste de barbeiro musical". A ilusão convence mais quando as notas são curtas e separadas. O compositor Jean-Claude Risset criou uma versão em que o som desliza sem degraus, e fez o mesmo com o ritmo, que parece acelerar sem fim. Em "Super Mario 64", de 1996, uma versão do tom acompanha a escada que nunca acaba no castelo da princesa Peach. Christopher Nolan o usou em "Dunkirk", de 2017, para criar uma tensão que parece só aumentar. No filme "A Odisseia", de 2026, também de Nolan, o compositor Ludwig Göransson usou um ritmo de Risset que acelera continuamente.

fontes.trecho: A Shepard tone, named after Roger Shepard, is a sound consisting of a superposition of sine waves separated by octaves. When played with the bass pitch of the tone moving upward or downward, it is referred to as the Shepard scale. This creates the auditory illusion of a tone that seems to continually ascend or descend in pitch, yet which ultimately gets no higher or lower. [...] Overlapping notes that play at the same time are exactly one octave apart, and each scale fades in and fades out so that hearing the beginning or end of any given scale is impossible. [...] the twelfth tone would be a loud B4 and an almost inaudible B5 with the addition of an almost inaudible B3. The thirteenth tone would then be the same as the first, and the cycle could continue indefinitely. [...] The theory behind the illusion was demonstrated during an episode of the BBC's show Bang Goes the Theory, where the effect was described as "a musical barber's pole". [...] The illusion is more convincing if there is a short time between successive notes (staccato or marcato rather than legato or portamento). [...] Jean-Claude Risset subsequently created a version of the scale where the tones glide continuously [...] Risset has also created a similar effect with rhythm in which tempo seems to increase or decrease endlessly. [...] In the video game Super Mario 64 (1996) for the Nintendo 64 console, a piece that plays when the player tries to climb the neverending stairs (before reaching 70 stars) located in the penultimate room of Peach's Castle incorporates a slightly modified Shepard scale played in the background. [...] This is fully realised in his 2017 film Dunkirk where a Shepard tone is used to create the illusion of an ever increasing moment of intensity across intertwined storylines. [...] The technique was used in Christopher Nolan's 2026 film The Odyssey. Composer Ludwig Göransson incorporated a continuously accelerating Risset rhythm into the score, which Nolan described as the rhythmic equivalent of a Shepard tone.

gancho: A obra musical escrita quase completa mais antiga que se conhece é um hino de cerca de 1400 a.C., em tabuleta de argila achada na Síria. A escrita é legível, mas há ao menos cinco versões rivais de como ele soava.
explicacao: Nos anos 1950, escavações no palácio real de Ugarit, cidade antiga no norte da Síria, revelaram fragmentos de tabuletas de argila com cerca de 36 hinos em escrita cuneiforme, numa camada do século XIV a.C. Só um deles, um hino a Nikkal, deusa dos pomares, chegou até nós quase inteiro, e por isso é considerado a obra musical notada substancialmente completa mais antiga do mundo. Ele antecede em cerca de mil anos outras músicas antigas conhecidas, como o Epitáfio de Seikilos. A tabuleta traz a letra em hurrita e, abaixo, instruções em acádio para um cantor acompanhado por um instrumento de nove cordas, muito provavelmente uma lira: nomes de intervalos seguidos de números. O nó está aí. As diferenças entre as transcrições dependem de como se interpretam esses pares de sinais e de como eles se ligam ao texto. As primeiras reconstruções leram a escala de cabeça para baixo, com as notas mais agudas virando as mais graves. Hoje há pelo menos cinco decifrações rivais, que produzem resultados completamente diferentes, embora a escrita em si seja bem compreendida e quase sem ambiguidade. A primeira execução moderna foi em 1974, e a tabuleta pertence ao Museu Nacional de Damasco.

fontes.trecho: The Hurrian songs (or Hurrian Hymns) are a collection of music written in cuneiform on clay tablets excavated from the ancient city of Ugarit, a headland in northern Syria, which date to approximately 1400 BCE. One of these tablets, which is nearly complete, contains the Hurrian Hymn to Nikkal [...] making it the oldest surviving substantially complete work of notated music in the world. [...] The complete song is one of about 36 such hymns in cuneiform writing, found on fragments of clay tablets excavated in the 1950s from the Royal Palace at Ugarit (present-day Ras Shamra, Syria), in a stratum dating from the fourteenth century BCE, but is the only one surviving in substantially complete form. [...] Tablet h.6 contains the lyrics for a hymn to Nikkal, an Ancient Near Eastern goddess of orchards, and instructions for a singer accompanied by a nine-stringed sammûm, a type of harp or, much more likely, a lyre. The hymn was given its first modern performance in 1974 [...] The Hurrian hymn pre-dates several other surviving early works of music (e.g., the Seikilos epitaph and the Delphic Hymns) by a millennium [...] The first reconstructions interpreted the musical scale upside down, with the highest tones incorrectly becoming the lowest. [...] this is only one of at least five "rival decipherments of the notation, each yielding entirely different results". These reconstructions (not decipherments in the correct sense of the word, because the script is well understood and mostly unambiguous) [...] The tablet is in the collection of the National Museum of Damascus. [...] Below this is found the Akkadian musical instructions, consisting of interval names followed by number signs. Differences in transcriptions hinge on interpretation of the meaning of these paired signs, and the relationship to the hymn text.

gancho: Ré, mi, fá, sol e lá (e o antigo "ut", hoje dó) saíram de um hino a São João. Com elas e com a pauta, o monge Guido d'Arezzo, no século XI, encurtou o treino de um cantor de 10 anos para um ou dois.
explicacao: Guido, monge beneditino italiano nascido entre 990 e 999, é tido como inventor, ou para alguns aperfeiçoador, da pauta musical moderna. Na abadia de Pomposa, ele reclamava do tempo enorme que os cantores gastavam decorando melodias e propôs um sistema que dispensaria a memorização. Os métodos novos despertaram o ressentimento dos colegas, e ele se mudou em 1025 para Arezzo, onde passou a formar os cantores da catedral. Ali, o treino padrão de dez anos para um cantor caiu para um ou dois. Um dos recursos era um mnemônico. No hino latino "Ut queant laxis", em honra de São João Batista, cada meio verso da primeira estrofe começa uma nota acima do anterior, e as sílabas iniciais, ut, re, mi, fa, sol, la, viraram os nomes das seis notas. O "ut" foi trocado na Itália, nos anos 1600, pelo "dó", de som mais aberto. Como o sistema de Guido tinha só seis notas, a sétima ganhou depois o nome "si", tirado de "Sancte Iohannes", as palavras do último verso. A fama do método chegou ao papa João XIX, que chamou Guido a Roma para explicá-lo ao clero.

fontes.trecho: A monk from the Order of Saint Benedict, he is regarded as the inventor—or by some, developer—of the modern staff notation [...] By around 1013 he began teaching at Pomposa Abbey, but his antiphonary Prologus in antiphonarium and novel teaching methods based on staff notation brought considerable resentment from his colleagues. He thus moved to Arezzo in 1025 and under the patronage of Bishop Tedald of Arezzo he taught singers at the Arezzo Cathedral. [...] Interested in his innovations, Pope John XIX called him to Rome. After arriving and beginning to explain his methods to the clergy [...] Guido was born sometime between 990 and 999. [...] In the prologue to the antiphonary, Guido expressed his frustration with the large amount of time singers spent to memorize music. The system, he explained, would prevent the need for memorization [...] Guido lessened the standard 10-year training for the ideal cantor to only one or two years.

is a Latin hymn in honor of John the Baptist [...] the first six musical phrases of each stanza begin on a successively higher notes of the hexachord, giving ut–re–mi–fa–so–la; though ut is replaced by do in modern solfège. The naming of the notes of the hexachord by the first syllable of each hemistich (half line of verse) of the first verse is usually attributed to Guido of Arezzo. [...] it was originally called "si" from "Sancte Ioannes" (Johannes).
"Ut" was changed in the 1600s in Italy to the open syllable "Do". Guido's system had only six notes, but "si" was added later as the seventh note of the diatonic scale.

gancho: Conta-se que a Igreja medieval proibia o trítono, o "intervalo do diabo", e punia quem o cantasse. Histórias de punição são provavelmente fantasia, e não se conhece nenhum registro medieval do apelido.
explicacao: O trítono é o intervalo de três tons inteiros, como de fá a si. Até o fim do Renascimento, a maioria dos teóricos o considerava instável e o rejeitava como consonância, e evitá-lo por razões musicais é prática antiga, que remonta ao organum paralelo do tratado medieval Musica Enchiriadis. Circula a lenda de que a Igreja o teria banido, chegando a excomungar cantores. Mas essas histórias de punição são, ao que tudo indica, fantasiosas. O próprio apelido "diabolus in musica" tem história curiosa. Os registros conhecidos vêm do século XVIII: Andreas Werckmeister o cita em 1702, Johann Joseph Fux em 1725 e Johann Mattheson em 1739, sempre atribuindo a expressão aos antigos. Ao contrário do que se repete, ninguém encontrou o termo em textos medievais. E a frase original encontrada, "mi contra fa est diabolus in musica", se referia à segunda menor, não ao trítono; Werckmeister a aplicava também ao choque entre notas como fá e fá sustenido. Há quem pense diferente: o musicólogo Denis Arnold sugere que o apelido já surgiu na própria música medieval, na época de Guido d'Arezzo. De todo modo, foi a associação simbólica com o diabo que levou a cultura ocidental a usar o trítono para sugerir o mal na música.

fontes.trecho: a tritone is a musical interval spanning three whole tones. For instance, the interval from F to the B above it (in short, F–B) is a tritone [...] From then until the end of the Renaissance, the tritone was regarded as an unstable interval and rejected as a consonance by most theorists. [...] being that the original found example of the term "diabolus en musica" is "Mi Contra Fa est diabolus en musica" ("Mi against Fa is the devil in music"), referring to the minor second. Andreas Werckmeister cites this term in 1702 as being used by "the old authorities" for both the tritone and for the clash between chromatically related tones such as F♮ and F♯ [...] Johann Joseph Fux cites the phrase in his seminal 1725 work Gradus ad Parnassum [...] and Johann Mattheson, in 1739, writes that the "older singers with solmization called this pleasant interval 'mi contra fa' or 'the devil in music'." Although the latter two of these authors cite the association with the devil as from the past, there are no known citations of this term from the Middle Ages, as is commonly asserted. However Denis Arnold, in the New Oxford Companion to Music, suggests that the nickname was already applied early in the medieval music itself [...] when Guido of Arezzo developed his system of hexachords [...] That original symbolic association with the devil and its avoidance led to Western cultural convention seeing the tritone as suggesting evil in music. However, stories that singers were excommunicated or otherwise punished by the Church for invoking this interval are likely fanciful. At any rate, avoidance of the interval for musical reasons has a long history, stretching back to the parallel organum of the Musica Enchiriadis.

gancho: Vivaldi morreu pobre e foi quase esquecido por dois séculos: nem "As Quatro Estações" eram conhecidas na edição original. A volta dele deve muito a uma falsificação e a volumes achados num mosteiro em 1926.
explicacao: Em vida, Vivaldi foi popular em muitos países da Europa, mas acabou indo para Viena atrás do apoio do imperador Carlos VI, que morreu logo depois da sua chegada, e o compositor morreu na pobreza menos de um ano mais tarde. Depois do Barroco, seus concertos publicados ficaram praticamente ignorados, e As Quatro Estações, hoje a obra mais famosa dele, eram desconhecidas na edição original durante os períodos clássico e romântico. A virada veio no começo do século XX, por um caminho torto. O violinista Fritz Kreisler fez passar por obra original de Vivaldi um Concerto em Dó que ele mesmo tinha escrito no estilo do italiano, e a peça levou o estudioso francês Marc Pincherle a pesquisar a fundo a obra de Vivaldi. Kreisler só revelou a autoria desses pastiches, atribuídos também a Tartini e Pugnani, em 1935. Quando críticos reclamaram, respondeu que eles mesmos já as tinham julgado valiosas: "O nome muda, o valor fica". Em 1926, num mosteiro do Piemonte, pesquisadores acharam volumes encadernados de Vivaldi que se julgavam perdidos nas Guerras Napoleônicas, com 300 concertos e 19 óperas, entre outras obras. Muitos manuscritos redescobertos foram comprados pela Biblioteca Nacional Universitária de Turim com o patrocínio de dois empresários da cidade, Roberto Foa e Filippo Giordano, em memória dos filhos.

fontes.trecho: After meeting the Emperor Charles VI, he moved to Vienna, hoping for royal support, but the emperor died soon after his arrival, and Vivaldi died in poverty less than a year later. After almost two centuries of decline, Vivaldi's musical reputation underwent a revival in the early 20th century [...] During his lifetime, Vivaldi was popular in many countries throughout Europe, including France, but after his death his popularity dwindled. After the end of the Baroque period, Vivaldi's published concerti became relatively unknown, and were largely ignored. Even his most famous work, The Four Seasons, was unknown in its original edition during the Classical and Romantic periods. [...] In the early 20th century, Fritz Kreisler's Concerto in C, in the Style of Vivaldi (which he passed off as an original Vivaldi work) helped revive Vivaldi's reputation. Kreisler's concerto in C spurred the French scholar Marc Pincherle to begin an academic study of Vivaldi's oeuvre. Many Vivaldi manuscripts were rediscovered, and were acquired by the Turin National University Library as a result of the generous sponsorship of Turinese businessmen Roberto Foa and Filippo Giordano, in memory of their sons. [...] In 1926, in a monastery in Piedmont, researchers discovered fourteen bound volumes of Vivaldi's work (later discovered to be fifteen) that were previously thought to have been lost during the Napoleonic Wars. [...] The volumes contained 300 concertos, 19 operas and over 100 vocal-instrumental works.

Some of Kreisler's compositions were pastiches ostensibly in the style of other composers. They were originally ascribed to earlier composers, such as Gaetano Pugnani, Giuseppe Tartini and Antonio Vivaldi, and then,  in 1935, Kreisler revealed that it was he who wrote the pieces. When critics complained, Kreisler replied that they had already deemed the compositions worthy: "The name changes, the value remains", he said.

gancho: Dias depois do enterro de Haydn, em 1809, dois adeptos da frenologia subornaram o coveiro e levaram a cabeça do compositor. O crânio só se juntou ao corpo em 1954, e o túmulo dele guarda hoje dois crânios.
explicacao: Haydn morreu em Viena em 31 de maio de 1809, aos 77 anos, com a cidade ocupada pelas tropas de Napoleão, e teve um funeral simples. Logo depois, Joseph Carl Rosenbaum, ex-secretário da família Esterházy, para quem Haydn trabalhara, e Johann Nepomuk Peter, diretor de uma prisão, pagaram ao coveiro para cortar e roubar a cabeça. Os dois admiravam Franz Joseph Gall e a frenologia, teoria hoje desacreditada que tentava ligar capacidades mentais à anatomia do crânio, e que se interessava especialmente pelos gênios. Depois do exame, Peter concluiu que a "protuberância da música" era de fato bem desenvolvida. Em 1820, o príncipe Nikolaus Esterházy II mandou exumar o corpo para levá-lo a Eisenstadt e achou uma peruca sobre o pescoço cortado. Os ladrões escaparam com várias manobras, incluindo crânios falsos. Durante uma busca na casa de Rosenbaum, o crânio estava escondido num colchão de palha, e a mulher dele se deitou na cama dizendo estar menstruada, o que manteve os investigadores longe. Por fim, ele entregou ao príncipe um outro crânio. O verdadeiro passou de mão em mão até chegar, em 1895, à Sociedade dos Amigos da Música de Viena. Só em 1954 ele foi levado ao túmulo na Bergkirche de Eisenstadt, encerrando um enterro de 145 anos. O crânio substituto não foi retirado.

fontes.trecho: The skull of composer Joseph Haydn was stolen shortly after his death in 1809; the perpetrators were interested in examining it for purposes of phrenology. [...] only in 1954 was it reunified for burial with the rest of Haydn's remains. [...] Haydn died in Vienna, aged 77, on 31 May 1809, after a long illness. As Austria was at war and Vienna occupied by Napoleon's troops,  a rather simple funeral was held [...] Following the burial, two men conspired to bribe the gravedigger and thereby sever and steal the dead composer's head. These were Joseph Carl Rosenbaum, a former secretary of the Esterházy family (Haydn's employers), and Johann Nepomuk Peter, governor of the provincial prison of Lower Austria. [...] Peter and Rosenbaum's motivation was an interest in phrenology, a now-discredited scientific movement that attempted to associate mental capacities with aspects of cranial anatomy; Peter and Rosenbaum were acquainted with and admired the work of Franz Joseph Gall, a leading phrenologist. Of particular interest to phrenology was the anatomy of individuals held to have exhibited great genius during their lifetime. [...] Peter concluded that "the bump of music" in Haydn's skull was indeed "fully developed". [...] In 1820, Haydn's old patron Prince Nikolaus Esterházy II [...] having Haydn's remains transferred from Gumpendorf to the family seat in Eisenstadt. Upon exhumation, they found a body with a wig above its severed neck. Haydn's head was missing. [...] However, through a series of devious maneuvers (blaming a deceased doctor, two fake skulls; one rejected) Peter and Rosenbaum managed to maintain possession of the skull. Rosenbaum hid the skull in a straw mattress. During the search of Rosenbaum's house, his wife Therese lay on the bed and claimed to be menstruating—with the result that the searchers did not go near the mattress. Eventually Rosenbaum gave Prince Esterházy a different skull. [...] After Rosenbaum's death in 1829, the skull passed from hand to hand. [...] Carl von Rokitansky who in 1895 gave it to the Vienna Gesellschaft der Musikfreunde (Society of the Friends of Music). [...] it was only in 1954 that the skull could be transferred, in a splendid ceremony, from the Gesellschaft der Musikfreunde to this tomb, thus completing the 145-year-long burial process. When the composer's skull was finally restored to the remainder of his skeleton, the substitute skull was not removed. Thus Haydn's tomb now contains two skulls.

A side chapel is dominated by a large marble sarcophagus, the tomb of the composer Joseph Haydn [...] The remains of most of Haydn's body have rested here since 1932; the skull was added (with due pomp and ceremony) only in 1954

gancho: Em 2015, um musicólogo achou num arquivo de Praga uma cantata perdida composta em parceria por Mozart, Salieri e um terceiro autor. É uma pista de que os dois "rivais" podiam ter uma relação amigável.
explicacao: A peça, "Per la ricuperata salute di Ofelia" (pela saúde recuperada de Ofélia), é de 1785 e celebrava a volta da soprano Nancy Storace, que tinha perdido a voz temporariamente e levou três meses para se recuperar. Ela interpretava obras dos dois compositores e seria a primeira Susanna de "As Bodas de Fígaro". O libreto é de Lorenzo Da Ponte, poeta da corte de Viena. A cantata, para soprano e fortepiano, dura uns quatro minutos e tem três partes, cada uma de um compositor: Salieri, Mozart e um certo Cornetti, cuja identidade ainda é especulada. A música era considerada perdida até novembro de 2015, quando o musicólogo alemão Timo Jouko Herrmann a identificou nos arquivos do Museu Tcheco da Música, em Praga, enquanto procurava obras de um suposto aluno de Salieri. Os nomes dos autores apareciam num tipo de código de assinatura comum na época. Para um diretor da Fundação Mozarteum, a imagem pintada pelo filme "Amadeus" é falsa: Salieri não envenenou Mozart, embora os dois trabalhassem em Viena e fossem concorrentes. O crítico Alex Ross foi menos entusiasmado com a obra: para ele, a história por trás da música interessa mais do que a própria música.

fontes.titulo: Per la ricuperata salute di Ofelia
fontes.trecho: Per la ricuperata salute di Ofelia (For the recovered health of Ophelia), K.6 477a, is a solo cantata for soprano and fortepiano composed in 1785 by Antonio Salieri and Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, and a third, unknown composer, Cornetti, to a libretto written by the Vienna court poet Lorenzo Da Ponte. It is speculated that "Cornetti" may refer to [...] The music had been considered lost until November 2015, when German musicologist and composer Timo Jouko Herrmann identified the score while searching for music by one of Salieri's ostensible pupils, Antonio Casimir Cartellieri, in the archives of the Czech Museum of Music in Prague. [...] Conceived, written and composed to celebrate the newly recovered health of Nancy Storace, the Vienna-based, Anglo-Italian soprano destined to become the first Susanna of Figaro, and to welcome her back to the stage after a temporary loss of her singing voice [...] the short work is compelling evidence of what may indeed have been an amicable and cooperative relationship between Salieri and Mozart. The brisk, four-minute cantata consists of three parts, each by a different composer. Madame Storace was known for interpreting works by both Mozart and Salieri, as well as by her brother. [...] Her recovery took three months. [...] bearing the names of Mozart and Salieri "in a kind of signature code that was common at the time," [...] Ulrich Leisinger, Director of the Research Department at the International Mozarteum Foundation, has said: We all know the picture drawn by the movie Amadeus. It is false. Salieri did not poison Mozart, but they both worked in Vienna and were competitors... [...] As for the cantata's artistic merits, Alex Ross observed in The New Yorker, ...(T)he story behind the music...holds more interest than the music itself

gancho: Por treze anos, a milionária russa Nadejda von Meck sustentou Tchaikovsky com uma mesada generosa, e os dois trocaram mais de 1.200 cartas. A condição dela era que nunca se encontrassem.
explicacao: Viúva de um engenheiro que ficou milionário construindo ferrovias, von Meck era uma pianista competente e, após a morte do marido, passou a viver quase reclusa. Começou encomendando peças a Tchaikovsky e depois lhe deu uma mesada de 6.000 rublos por ano, o bastante para ele largar o posto de professor no Conservatório de Moscou e se dedicar só a compor. Para comparar, um funcionário público de baixo escalão sustentava a família com 300 a 400 rublos anuais. Entre 1877 e 1890, os dois trocaram mais de 1.200 cartas, e ele se abriu com ela sobre a vida e o processo criativo como com nenhuma outra pessoa. Tchaikovsky lhe dedicou a Sinfonia nº 4. Quase nunca se viram: em Florença, ele via o cortejo dela passar todas as manhãs, e uma vez se avistaram de longe na ópera, encontro talvez arranjado por ela. Em 1879, na propriedade dela, os dois se cruzaram por acaso num bosque: ele tirou o chapéu, ninguém disse nada, e à noite ele escreveu pedindo desculpas pela quebra do combinado. Em outubro de 1890, von Meck mandou um ano de mesada adiantado, com uma carta que encerrava o patrocínio, alegando falência. Na época, estava gravemente doente, com tuberculose, e sob pressão dos filhos, que se incomodavam com a relação. Ela também contratou um jovem Claude Debussy como professor de música das filhas. Ele quis se casar com uma delas, e a mãe não deu permissão.

fontes.trecho: She is best known today for her artistic relationship with Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky, supporting him financially for thirteen years, so that he could devote himself full-time to composition, while stipulating that they were never to meet. Tchaikovsky dedicated his Symphony No. 4 in F minor to her. [...] A serious student of music in her youth, Nadezhda became a capable pianist [...] his investments made him a multi-millionaire. The railway lines for which he was responsible included [...] After the death of her husband, von Meck took no part in social life, withdrawing into almost complete seclusion. [...] She hired Claude Debussy as a music tutor for her daughters, and he wanted to marry one of them. She would not give her permission [...] she commissioned some pieces for violin and piano to be played at her house. [...] she subsequently provided him with an allowance of 6,000 rubles a year, large enough that he could leave his professorship at the Moscow Conservatory to focus on creative work full-time. This was a substantial income. A minor government official in those days had to support his family on 300–400 rubles a year. [...] They carried on a significant correspondence, exchanging over 1,200 letters between 1877 and 1890. The details they shared were extraordinary for two people who never met. He was more open to her about much of his life and his creative processes than to any other person. [...] while staying at her villa in Florence, Tchaikovsky had seen her and her entourage pass by every morning; and they also glimpsed each other once at the opera, but only from a distance. Alexander Poznansky says of this last encounter: "It is not clear whether their both being at the theater was wholly accidental or arranged by Mrs. von Meck in order to see him, as seems not unlikely." [...] In October 1890, von Meck sent Tchaikovsky a year's allowance in advance, along with a letter ending her patronage. She claimed bankruptcy. [...] By 1890, she was gravely ill.  She was in the latter stages of tuberculosis [...] She was under intense family pressure to end the relationship. Her children were embarrassed by her closeness with Tchaikovsky. [...] The two did meet on one occasion, purely by chance, in August 1879, while Tchaikovsky was staying at the von Meck estate at Simaki.

gancho: Benjamin Franklin inventou em 1761 um instrumento de tigelas de vidro girando num eixo, para o qual Mozart compôs. Em terras alemãs, correu o boato de que ele enlouquecia músicos e ouvintes.
explicacao: Franklin teve a ideia depois de ver, em 1761, taças de vinho com água sendo tocadas em Cambridge, na Inglaterra. Com um vidreiro de Londres, criou um arranjo radicalmente novo: na versão dele, 37 tigelas ficavam enfileiradas na horizontal num eixo de ferro, girado por um pedal, e o som saía por atrito. Chamou a invenção de armonica, do italiano armonia, e descreveu seus tons como "incomparavelmente doces". O instrumento fez sucesso: mais de cem compositores escreveram para ele, entre eles Mozart, em 1791, e Beethoven o usou numa obra de 1814. Franz Anton Mesmer, o do mesmerismo, fazia dele parte central do seu método. A popularidade, porém, não passou muito do século XVIII. Uma explicação é o volume baixo, fácil de abafar por outros instrumentos. Outra seriam boatos de que tocá-lo enlouquecia músicos e plateias, ao que parece restritos à Alemanha, talvez só a Viena. Um musicólogo alemão chegou a escrever que ele afundava o tocador numa melancolia que era um método de "lenta autoaniquilação". Uma versão moderna diz que os músicos se envenenavam com o chumbo do vidro, mas não há base científica conhecida para isso. Na época, o chumbo estava por toda parte, de remédios a utensílios de cozinha e até à tinta que marcava as tigelas, e o pouco que viesse do vidro provavelmente era irrelevante perto disso.

fontes.trecho: a type of musical instrument that uses a series of glass bowls or goblets graduated in size to produce musical tones by means of friction [...] It was invented in 1761 by Benjamin Franklin and produces sound that is ethereal and haunting [...] When Benjamin Franklin invented his mechanical version of the instrument in 1761, he called it the armonica, based on the Italian word armonia, which means "harmony". [...] Benjamin Franklin invented a radically new arrangement of the glasses in 1761 after seeing water-filled wine glasses played by Edward Delaval at Cambridge in England in May 1761. Franklin worked with London glassblower Charles James to build one [...] "The advantages of this instrument are, that its tones are incomparably sweet beyond those of any other [...] In Franklin's treadle-operated version, 37 bowls were mounted horizontally on an iron spindle. The whole spindle turned by means of a foot pedal. [...] Franz Mesmer also played the armonica and used it as an integral part of his Mesmerism. [...] and more than 100 others composed works for the glass harmonica [...] Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart wrote his 1791 K. 617 and K.356 (K.617a) for the glass harmonica. Ludwig van Beethoven used the instrument in his 1814 melodrama Leonore Prohaska. [...] The instrument's popularity did not last far beyond the 18th century. This may have been due to the inability to amplify the volume so as not to be drowned out by other instruments. Some claim this was due to strange rumors that using the instrument caused both musicians and their listeners to go mad. It is a matter of conjecture how pervasive that belief was; all the commonly cited examples of this rumor seem to be German, if not confined to Vienna. One example of alleged effects from playing the glass harmonica was noted by German musicologist Johann Friedrich Rochlitz [...] plunges the player into a nagging depression and hence into a dark and melancholy mood, that is an apt method for slow self-annihilation. [...] A modern version of the "purported dangers" claims that players suffered lead poisoning because armonicas were made of lead glass. However, there is no known scientific basis for the theory that merely touching lead glass can cause lead poisoning. [...] doctors prescribed lead compounds for a long list of ailments, and lead or lead oxide was used as a food preservative and in cookware and eating utensils. Trace amounts of lead that armonica players in Franklin's day received from their instruments would likely have been dwarfed by lead from other sources [...] would likely have been dwarfed by lead from other sources, such as the lead-content paint used to mark visual identification of the bowls to the players

gancho: A voz de um castrato não é só lenda: Alessandro Moreschi, do coro da Capela Sistina, gravou discos em 1902 e 1904. Foi o único castrato a gravar solos, bem quando um papa mandou trocar essas vozes por meninos.
explicacao: Por séculos, meninos com talento vocal eram castrados bem antes da puberdade para manter a voz aguda. Moreschi nasceu em 1858 perto de Frascati, nos Estados Papais. Talvez tenha sido castrado por causa de uma hérnia, já que a castração ainda era vista como cura na Itália do século XIX, ou talvez por volta de 1865, segundo a prática antiga. Ele virou primeiro soprano da Capela Sistina, posto que ocupou por trinta anos, e era a única esperança de manter ali a tradição do célebre Miserere de Allegri: os outros seis castrati do coro não davam conta da parte aguda. Em abril de 1902, os irmãos Gaisberg, da Gramophone & Typewriter Company, de Londres, montaram o equipamento numa sala do Vaticano de paredes cobertas de Ticianos e Rafaéis e gravaram o coro, incluindo quatro solos de Moreschi. Em 1904 houve uma segunda sessão, e as gravações dele somam dezessete faixas. Em novembro de 1903, o novo papa, Pio X, determinou que as partes de soprano e contralto fossem cantadas por meninos, e Moreschi e os poucos colegas restantes deveriam ser aposentados. Ele seguiu oficialmente no coro até 1913. Os críticos divergem sobre os discos: uns ouvem um cantor medíocre; outros, o que restava de um cantor talentoso.

fontes.trecho: Alessandro Moreschi (1 November 1858 – 21 April 1922) was an Italian chorister of the late 19th century and the only castrato to make solo recordings. [...] the town of Monte Compatri in the Papal States, near Frascati (Lazio). It is possible that he was born with an inguinal hernia, for which castration was still thought to be a cure in 19th-century Italy. Another possibility is that he was castrated later, around 1865, which would have been more in line with the centuries-old practice of castrating vocally talented boys well before puberty. [...] he was appointed First Soprano there, a post he held for the next thirty years. [...] realised that Moreschi was, amongst other things, the only hope for the continuation of the Sistine tradition of performing the famous setting of the Miserere by Gregorio Allegri during Holy Week. When Moreschi joined the Sistine choir, there were still six other castrato members, but none of them were capable of sustaining this work's taxing soprano tessitura. [...] He made additional recordings in 1904 with seventeen tracks total. [...] His successor was Pope Pius X, a powerful advocate of Cecilianism. Among the pontiff's first official acts was the promulgation of the motu proprio, Tra le sollecitudini ("Amidst the Cares") on St Cecilia's Day, 22 November 1903, stating: "Whenever ... it is desirable to employ the high voices of sopranos and contraltos, these parts must be taken by boys, according to the most ancient usage of the Church." Moreschi and his few remaining colleagues were to be pensioned and replaced by boys. Officially, Alessandro was a member of the Sistine choir until Easter 1913 [...] The first series of recordings was made on 3 and 5 April 1902 by Will and Fred Gaisberg. Eighteen usable sides by the members of the Sistine Chapel Choir were captured on wax, four of them solos by Moreschi. [...] "Selecting a great salon with walls covered with Titians, Raphaels, and Tintorettos, we mounted our grimy machine right in the middle of the floor." The second set of recordings was made in Rome in April 1904 [...] Some say they are of little interest other than the novelty of preserving the voice of a castrato, and that Moreschi was a mediocre singer, while others detect the remains of a talented singer

gancho: A gravação mais antiga de música tocada por computador, de 1951, soava no tom errado. Pesquisadores notaram isso porque ela tinha notas que a máquina do laboratório de Turing jamais conseguiria produzir.
explicacao: Em 1951, uma equipe externa da BBC gravou num disco de acetato três melodias tocadas pelo enorme computador do laboratório de Alan Turing, em Manchester: o hino nacional britânico, a cantiga "Baa, Baa, Black Sheep" e "In the Mood", de Glenn Miller. A máquina tinha uma instrução que soltava um pulso curto no alto-falante; repetida em certos padrões, a sequência de cliques soava como uma nota contínua. Turing usava esses sons para indicar o que o computador estava fazendo, e foi o jovem professor Christopher Strachey quem, numa noite sozinho na máquina, programou o hino. Segundo Jack Copeland e o compositor Jason Long, é mito a ideia de que as primeiras notas de computador soaram em 1957 nos EUA: no laboratório de Turing, elas já saíam do alto-falante no outono de 1948. O computador foi sucateado há muito tempo, e o disco é a única janela para o seu som. Os dois calcularam, a partir do manual de programação de Turing, todas as frequências que a máquina podia gerar e viram que muitas das que o disco tocava eram impossíveis para ela. A diferença revelou a velocidade errada, provavelmente porque o prato do gravador portátil girava rápido demais. Corrigida a velocidade e filtrado o ruído, pesquisadores da Universidade de Canterbury, na Nova Zelândia, restauraram o som em 2016.

fontes.titulo: Restoring the first recording of computer music (British Library, Sound and Vision blog)
fontes.trecho: An important case in point is the earliest known recording of computer-generated music. In 1951, a BBC outside broadcast unit in Manchester used a portable acetate disc cutter to capture three melodies played by a primeval computer. This gigantic computer filled much of the ground floor of Alan Turing's Computing Machine Laboratory.
